cards.f: Ways to reduce environmental impact of technology
cards.b: Energy-efficient hardware, renewable energy for data centres, recycle or reuse devices, repair rather than replace, power-saving settings.
The gap between people who have access to technology and the internet and those who do not, due to cost, location, age or disability.
Personal data (location, browsing, purchases) may be collected, tracked, sold, leaked or hacked, and surveillance reduces anonymity.
Being honest, competent and responsible: protecting data, respecting copyright, testing software properly and following a code of conduct.
Legal right that gives the creator of an original work control over copying and distributing it. Copying without permission is piracy.
Legal protection for an invention that stops others making or selling it without permission for a limited time.
Open source: source code freely available to view, modify and share. Proprietary: paid licence, code kept secret, cannot be copied or changed.
A virus attaches to a file and spreads when it is opened. A worm spreads by itself across a network.
Malware that encrypts the user's files and demands payment to unlock them.
Fake emails or messages that look genuine, tricking people into giving personal details or clicking harmful links.
Redirecting users from a real website to a fake one, even when they type the correct address, to steal their details.
Watching someone enter a password or PIN by looking over their shoulder.
An authorised attempt to break into a system to find weaknesses so they can be fixed before real attackers find them.
A record (log) of actions carried out on a system and who did them, used to detect and investigate misuse.

short.q: Describe the difference between a virus and a worm.
short.model: A virus attaches itself to a file or program and spreads when the user runs it. A worm spreads by itself across a network without any user action.
points: virus needs a host file/user action to spread
worm spreads by itself across networks

short.q: Explain two ways a school could protect its network from cyber-attacks.
short.model: Use a firewall to block unauthorised traffic, and give users different access levels with strong passwords so they can only reach the data they need. Regular updates and staff training also help.
points: measure 2 with a reason it helps (e.g. access levels, passwords, training)

short.q: Give two reasons why AI raises ethical concerns.
short.model: AI can be biased if trained on unrepresentative data, which leads to unfair decisions. It can also replace jobs and raise questions about who is responsible when it makes a mistake.
points: job losses or responsibility for errors

short.q: A company sells software under a proprietary licence. State two things that users are not allowed to do.
short.model: Users may not copy and share the software, and they may not change it or see its source code.
points: copy / share / install on unlimited machines
modify or access the source code

short.q: Explain why quantum computing could be a threat to data security.
short.model: Quantum computers may solve some problems much faster, so they could break current encryption methods and expose protected data. New types of encryption would be needed.
points: quantum computers could break current encryption
data protected by it would be at risk / new methods needed
